overview.title: Encode Tiny Shakespeare with the GPT-2 tokenizer
overview.summary: The same plays as the character dataset, packed as GPT-2 tokens instead of single characters.

sections.title: Download, split, encode, and save
sections.pseudocode:
Download Tiny Shakespeare and write input.txt when it is missing.
Cut at 0.9, encode both sides with the gpt2 tokenizer, and save uint16 bins.
# Insight: No codec file is written. Decoding later assumes GPT-2.

logic.title: Encode Tiny Shakespeare with the GPT-2 tokenizer
logic.summary: Download the plays, split them, and write GPT-2 token ids for a small fine-tune.

sections.title: Download the text if it is missing
sections.pseudocode:
Look for input.txt next to this script.
If it is missing, download Tiny Shakespeare.
Write that text to input.txt.

sections.title: Hold out the last tenth, then encode
sections.pseudocode:
Read the file.
Cut at 0.9 of the characters.
Keep the head as train and the tail as validation.
Load the gpt2 tokenizer.
Encode both splits, ignoring special tokens.
Print how many tokens each split holds.
Store the ids as uint16.
Write train.bin and val.bin next to this script.
# Insight: There is no meta.pkl. sample.py will assume GPT-2 encodings, which matches this tokenizer.
# Context: encode_ordinary skips special tokens such as the end-of-text marker. The character-level prepare script does not use this tokenizer at all.
